headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP and context handling can amplify prompt injection and data leakage when paired with Airflow’s broad egress, but no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and user-facing agent interface, so it can ingest external content; Airflow has broad network egress and can move data between tasks. No shared channel is documented, but if Airflow outputs are routed into MemMachine via MCP or copied into its context, instruction hijacking is plausible.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is forwarded into MemMachine via MCP or API
IF MemMachine treats retrieved content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Disable automatic ingestion of Airflow logs into MemMachine
Require human review before MemMachine acts on Airflow output
Use a read-only summary channel instead of raw task text

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Airflow has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, any workflow that passes Airflow artifacts into MemMachine can expose sensitive context to a component that may transmit data outward through its API surfaces.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs contain sensitive operational data
IF those outputs are stored in or forwarded to MemMachine context
mitigations: Strip secrets and identifiers before handoff
Limit MemMachine context to minimal summaries
Block Airflow logs from being sent to external APIs
Rotate any credentials that may appear in task output

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress, while MemMachine offers REST, Python SDK, and MCP access. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or OAuth scopes, so direct resource contention is not evidenced; the main overlap is coordination, not conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource
IF an orchestrator does not provide locking or serialization
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Use a single writer for shared resources
Add lock files or queue-based serialization
Restrict one agent to read-only access

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can consume conversational context and act through API/MCP surfaces, so it may treat Airflow-produced text as authoritative if wired together. Airflow can generate operational outputs, but no verification boundary between the agents is documented, making a mistaken handoff a realistic default-path cascade rather than a proven high-impact automation chain.
conditions: IF Airflow output is used as input to MemMachine without validation
IF MemMachine is allowed to act on that input automatically
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Airflow outputs
Mark Airflow output as untrusted in MemMachine prompts
Disable automatic downstream actions from MemMachine

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow’s profile shows no touched data classes, while MemMachine explicitly handles long-term user facts and conversational context. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to a potential policy gap if sensitive user context is routed through Airflow-managed pipelines.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through Airflow into MemMachine
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Document the data classification for each handoff
Exclude regulated data from the pair
Set a shared retention policy for routed context
Add deletion/export procedures for MemMachine-held context
